sources.title: robots.txt for https://www.homedepot.com/
sources.owner: The Home Depot, Inc. (Homer TLC, Inc.)
sources.data_provided: Crawler directives; points to sitemap https://www.homedepot.com/sitemap/main.xml (URL as reported in search summary).
sources.period_covered: Index date not stated; summary says two different versions of the file were indexed
sources.access_notes: Not fetched (blocked). Search summary reports User-agent: * rules disallowing checkout, cart, sign-in/account pages, internal search/navigation URLs (/SiteMapView, /CheckoutSignIn, /OrderItemUpdate, /THDLogon, /cart, /checkout*, /order-confirmation*) and paginated review pages except page 1.
sources.reuse_terms: Per search snippet: one rule set for all crawlers (User-agent: *); product-detail pages are not reported as disallowed, but robots.txt grants no reuse right and the (unseen) main-site Terms of Use govern. findings.statement: Per-retailer conclusion (all rest on search snippets only; none could be read live): Lowe's = prohibited (automated retrieval, data mining and reproduction barred; scraping defined as reseller activity in one version). Ferguson = prohibited (scraping/robots and collecting product listings, descriptions or prices excluded from license). Sherwin-Williams = restricted_no_automated_access (robot/scraper/spider/automated means banned; mirroring and public display barred). Home Depot = unknown_needs_check (main-site Terms of Use clause text not seen; a related Home Depot page says screen scraping is expressly prohibited; robots.txt disallows checkout/cart/search paths) - treat as restricted until a human reads the live page. Grainger = unknown_needs_check (Terms of Access exist and bind registrants, clause text not seen; Grainger filters bot traffic). Dunn-Edwards = unknown_needs_check (no terms or robots.txt found). Project rule consequence: no scraping/crawling of any of these sites; no login/CAPTCHA bypass; no accounts opened on the company's behalf; retailer prices enter the database only through a permitted route confirmed by a human (official program, or manual observation if the live terms allow it).
findings.evidence_quote: (Use any robot, spider, site search/retrieval application or other manual or automatic device or process to retrieve, index, data mine or in any way reproduce or circumvent the navigational structure or presentation of the Site or its contents)

findings.statement: A separate cached version of Lowe's terms defines 'reseller activities' to include scraping and gathering information from the Site in connection with the sale of products; which cached URL carries this text was not identified (candidates: https://www.lowes.com/l/terms-and-conditions-of-use.html, https://applianceparts.lowes.com/termsofuse).
findings.evidence_quote: A separate version of the terms defines reseller activities to include extracting, scraping, mining, copying or otherwise gathering information from the Site in connection with your sale or another party's sale of products.

findings.statement: Lowe's claims the compilation of all site content as its exclusive property under copyright and limits content use to viewing in connection with the site.
findings.evidence_quote: The compilation (meaning the collection, arrangement and assembly) of all content on the Site is the exclusive property of Lowe's and protected by applicable copyright laws.

findings.statement: Home Depot's robots.txt (as indexed) uses a single User-agent: * block disallowing checkout, cart, sign-in/account, and internal search/navigation URLs and lists a main sitemap; two different versions were seen. Absence of a Disallow for product pages is not permission.
findings.evidence_quote: The search snippets show two different versions of the file, one with plain paths and one with wildcard patterns, so the live file may have changed since these were indexed.

findings.topic: Home Depot main Terms of Use not retrieved
findings.statement: Three targeted searches failed to surface the homedepot.com Terms of Use text. Third-party scraping vendors assert the terms prohibit automated collection, but none quotes the clause, so this is not verified.
findings.evidence_quote: A SparkProxy guide says Home Depot's terms prohibit automated collection, and a separate guide repeats that the terms prohibit automated collection.

findings.statement: A scraper-tool vendor review reports a direct request to a Home Depot product page was denied (HTTP 403, AkamaiGHost), consistent with the sandbox 403s and with active bot management. Vendor claim, not verified.
findings.evidence_quote: One scraper-tool review says a direct request to a Home Depot product page returned HTTP 403 Access Denied from AkamaiGHost.

findings.topic: Third-party 'Home Depot API' scrapers are not a legitimate route
findings.statement: Commercial 'Home Depot API' and scraping services exist (e.g., BigBox API). A scraping vendor's own page acknowledges that scraping Home Depot data can violate Home Depot's terms; using an intermediary does not remove the site-terms exposure. Do not use.
findings.evidence_quote: One scraping-services page says that scraping Home Depot data can violate Home Depot's terms of service and suggests using official APIs or robots.txt compliance to reduce risk.

findings.statement: Ferguson's terms (reproduced on ferguson.com product pages) exclude scraping, robots, and collecting product listings, descriptions or prices from the personal-use license and bar use that could overburden the site.
findings.evidence_quote: The same clause also excludes collecting product listings, descriptions, or prices.

findings.statement: Sherwin-Williams' Terms of Use ban any robot, scraper, spider or other automated means to access or gather website content and bar mirroring/framing/public display.
findings.evidence_quote: That snippet lists a ban on using "any robot, scraper, spider, or other automated means" to access or gather content from its websites (iii).

findings.statement: Grainger's Terms of Access exist and registration binds users to them, but clause text was not found. Grainger publicly reports (Datadog case study) removing unwanted bot traffic, so automated access should be assumed unwelcome.
findings.evidence_quote: Account sign-up pages state that registering means agreeing to the Terms of Sale and Terms of Access.

findings.statement: Grainger documents (via an Indiana procurement overview) ERP integration, an API, Punch-Out (OCI/cXML) and EDI/XML transactions; all appear tied to a customer account and rep contact. Fees not stated. A public developer portal with open signup was not found.
findings.evidence_quote: Third-party platforms such as Precoro and Procurify require you to contact a Grainger representative with your account number to receive Punch-Out credentials.

findings.topic: Grainger API search came up empty
findings.statement: No Grainger developer portal, public API documentation, pricing or signup terms appeared in results; the only API mentions are in the eProcurement overview and an anecdotal forum post that Grainger has an API but recommends Punch-Out.
findings.evidence_quote: Fairmarkit's documentation describes a Grainger integration that is enabled through a Fairmarkit customer success manager and tied to a Grainger account number for customer-specific pricing.

findings.topic: Home Depot and Lowe's affiliate product feeds
findings.statement: Both retailers run affiliate programs (Home Depot on Impact; Lowe's on Impact per most sources, Rakuten per one) that list product data feeds among promotional tools. Feed field coverage (price, SKU, store-level pricing) and permitted uses are undocumented in results. These are promotional channels requiring an approved affiliate account; use as an internal cost-database feed is unverified and probably outside affiliate terms (inference).
findings.evidence_quote: One review says the program offers a daily product data feed, text links, and banner ads.

findings.statement: Home Depot PRO is available as a cXML punch-out supplier in procurement systems (university job aid, Precoro). It returns a buyer's cart with description/pricing/quantity into the requisition system; it is account-based, not a bulk price export. No public Home Depot API was found.
findings.evidence_quote: Precoro offers a Home Depot PunchOut connection. Its description says the integration automatically imports selected items and their details, such as descriptions, pricing, and quantities, into the procurement system for approval.

findings.topic: Cooperative contracts are discount schedules, not SKU price books
findings.statement: Sourcewell Facility MRO awards (Grainger 091422-WWG; Fastenal, HD Supply, Motion, NAPA/IBS, WESCO, MSC) publish discount structures off list/category pricing and freight terms; no public SKU price list surfaced. No Sourcewell contract for Home Depot retail or Ferguson was found. Grainger contract expiry is reported inconsistently (Nov 8, 2026 vs Nov 8, 2027), so status must be confirmed given today is 2026-10-24.
findings.evidence_quote: The bid comment notes that along with pre-paid freight, they are offering a substantial discount off category pricing.

findings.topic: GSA Advantage has no bulk export in results
findings.statement: Schedule price lists are published per contract (PDF/HTML at gsaadvantage.gov/ref_text/...), uploaded via the FAS Catalog Platform; no consolidated bulk dataset, SIN-level extract or reuse terms were found, and no building-materials schedule was identified.
findings.evidence_quote: The results do not describe a public bulk export of GSA Advantage pricing, a SIN-level data set, or reuse terms.

findings.topic: California DGS statewide contracts coverage is narrow
findings.statement: DGS results covered only a mandatory exterior recycled paint contract (SC 1-26-80-10); pricing/user instructions are on Cal eProcure rather than in the bulletin. No HVAC or general building-materials statewide price list was found.
findings.evidence_quote: The search turned up DGS paint contract notices but no consolidated price list, and nothing on HVAC supplies.

findings.statement: BLS Public Data API v2 requires free registration (email, organization; key from labstat@bls.gov) and allows 500 queries/day, 50 series/query, 20 years/query; it returns observations and footnotes only, not metadata. This is the cleanest legitimate machine route for construction-material price INDEXES (PPI), national scope only.
findings.evidence_quote: The API will only return observational values and footnotes. It does not return metadata.

findings.topic: Free price benchmarks are indexes, not unit prices
findings.statement: The only legitimately free benchmark datasets located are national indexes (BLS PPI via BLS API/FRED, including ready-mix concrete) and USGS national annual commodity statistics for cement and gypsum. No free dollar-per-unit regional (Los Angeles) building-material price dataset was found in this research. BLS reuse terms were not visible; USGS entries carry a U.S. Government Work note.
findings.evidence_quote: The search found USGS data releases for cement and gypsum, but none of the results gave an average price per metric ton, so you'll need to check the data sheets directly.

findings.topic: CSI MasterFormat is copyrighted and licensed
findings.statement: CSI states MasterFormat is copyright-protected and used under an EULA; commercial use in a derivative product that employs MasterFormat numbers or titles requires contacting CSI. Do not embed MasterFormat numbers/titles without a license; forum fee figures ($500 application, $1,100 minimum annual) are anecdotal.
findings.evidence_quote: Anyone using MasterFormat does so under the license granted by the MasterFormat End User License Agreement.

findings.statement: UniFormat's EULA (v. 9/3/2020) grants single-user online access only and requires different licenses for libraries, multiple users and downloads; OmniClass is licensed in three options with quote-priced organizational licenses. NBIMS-US has only a narrow license to publish select OmniClass tables. A secondary blog claims CSI moved MasterFormat/OmniClass/UniFormat to a digital-only licensing platform in February 2026 (unverified).
findings.evidence_quote: In February 2026, it announced the rollout of "The Construction Standard" (a digital-only platform – CSI Dynamic Standards, CDS)

findings.topic: Uniclass is a freely licensed alternative (secondary evidence)
findings.statement: A secondary blog states the UK Uniclass is under CC BY-ND 4.0. NoDerivatives means modified versions cannot be redistributed (prior-knowledge inference, unverified), so Uniclass could be referenced/cross-walked but not adapted and republished. Official NBS license page not seen.
findings.evidence_quote: The UK's Uniclass is different. It is licensed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution-NoDerivatives 4.0 International (CC BY-ND 4.0) licence.

findings.statement: UNSPSC can be browsed and downloaded free from unspsc.org; management reportedly moved from GS1 US to UNDP on 2025-01-01 (per a standards-catalog result); the commercial-use FAQ answer was not visible and the Data.gov copy states no license information. Treat as unknown until UNDP confirms.
findings.evidence_quote: A UNSPSC dataset on Data.gov is listed as "No license information was provided."

findings.statement: Census publishes the 2022 NAICS code list and crosswalks for download and BLS offers a CSV with titles and descriptions; the results did not state license terms (federal products are probably unrestricted - inference). NAICS classifies industries, not materials.
findings.evidence_quote: The Census Bureau's industry code lists page offers a 2022 NAICS industry code list, along with crosswalks, for download.

findings.statement: AHRI Directory has no public API; free users can export only the first 250 records to CSV; complete data requires a Data Subscription license, and most participants are classified commercial. Scraping the directory is outside the stated route.
findings.evidence_quote: No public API: AHRI's licensing page says API access is not available.

findings.topic: HVAC manufacturer spec sheets not surfaced
findings.statement: The HVAC search returned only Ferguson retail listings (Trane 5TTX6/5TTR6 R-454B, 13-17 SEER2 families) and no manufacturer submittal PDFs for Trane, Carrier, Goodman/Daikin or Lennox. Retail pages also conflict internally (a 4-ton Trane listing shows 'up to 18.0 SEER2' in the title and 'up to 17.1 SEER2' in the bullets), so they are unreliable for specs. Ferguson terms bar collecting its listings, so none recorded.
findings.evidence_quote: The 4-ton Trane listing gives both "Up to 18.0 SEER2" in the title and "Up to 17.1 SEER2" in its feature bullets.

findings.topic: Rebar weights can be cited or derived
findings.statement: ASTM A615 Table 1 values for #3-#5 were visible via an ANSI Webstore listing; the full standard is sold. Prior-knowledge (unverified): nominal weights follow from nominal area x steel density (about 3.4 lb/ft per in2), allowing independent derivation without reproducing ASTM text. Bar number equals nominal diameter in eighths of an inch.
findings.evidence_quote: The bar number is simply the nominal diameter in eighths of an inch, so #8 is one inch in diameter (multiply the bar size by 1/8 to get the nominal diameter in inches).

findings.statement: PS 20 (American Softwood Lumber Standard) with the National Grading Rule underpins dimension lumber sizes; ALSC authorizes grading agencies such as WWPA (Western Lumber Grading Rules book) and SPIB. NIST confirms nominal 2x4 = 1.5 x 3.5 in. Size tables and rule-book cost/license were not visible.
findings.evidence_quote: The U.S. Department of Commerce's American Softwood Lumber Standard PS 20 correlates lumber size to moisture content. It also provides for a National Grading Rule (NGR) for Dimension Lumber with simplified grade names and sizes.

findings.topic: Joint compound coverage figures conflict across sources
findings.statement: Retail listings relay 450 sq ft per 4.5 gal pail (all-purpose, midweight) and about 500 sq ft (lightweight), while a USG FAQ gives two pails per 1,000 sq ft for Ultra Lightweight. Use the manufacturer data sheet for each compound plus finish level; do not ingest retailer coverage text.
findings.evidence_quote: Manufacturer and retailer listings give conflicting coverage figures for USG Sheetrock ready-mix compounds, mostly in the 450 to 500 sq ft range per 4.5-gallon pail.

findings.statement: USG UltraLight 1/2 in. is 1.25 lb/sq ft versus 1.6 lb/sq ft for USG Regular 1/2 in.; National Gypsum Gold Bond High Strength LITE 1/2 in. is 1.3-1.4 lb/sq ft. A National Gypsum or USG standard 1/2 in. Type X data sheet, CertainTeed and Georgia-Pacific documents were not found.
findings.evidence_quote: Gold Bond High Strength LITE 1/2 in.: National Gypsum's construction guide lists Weight, Nominal 1.3 – 1.4 lbs/sq ft

findings.statement: Dunn-Edwards publishes per-product data sheets under dunnedwards.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/01/ and a 07/2026 conformance table. EVEREST sheets give 1.5 mil DFT and 375-425 sq ft/gal; the EVERSHIELD, VINYLASTIC and SPARTASHIELD snippets showed VOC/solids but no spread rate. Do not apply EVEREST coverage to other lines.
findings.evidence_quote: Don't apply those numbers to the Evershield or Spartashield lines without checking their own sheets.

findings.statement: Johns Manville's fact sheet is the most complete single coverage source found (R-13/R-19/R-30 batts, sq ft per bag, pieces per bag, compression note). Owens Corning coverage appeared only on retail/distributor listings.
findings.evidence_quote: Coverage figures differ by batt width, length, and thickness, so check the exact SKU on the manufacturer's current data sheet before ordering.

findings.topic: Legal context: robots.txt is voluntary but terms-of-use notice matters
findings.statement: A law-firm article notes robots.txt compliance is voluntary but its presence helps establish that bots were not impliedly licensed, and recommends that written demands attach the website terms. The project rule of honoring robots.txt AND the site terms is consistent with this commentary (not legal advice).
findings.evidence_quote: While compliance with robots.txt files is voluntary, inclusion of such files is often necessary to stop a court from later concluding that you impliedly licensed bots to access the site.

gaps: Live clause text for homedepot.com Terms of Use, Grainger Terms of Access, Ferguson terms landing page, Dunn-Edwards terms, and the full Sherwin-Williams terms could not be read (network blocked; search returns only summaries). A human must open the live pages and record verbatim clauses, effective dates and any robots.txt (Grainger, Ferguson, Sherwin-Williams, Dunn-Edwards robots.txt were not found).

Home Depot and Lowe's affiliate programs: actual feed terms, field list (does it include price, store-level availability, SKU/model), permitted uses, and whether an internal cost database is a permitted use are unknown; network for Lowe's conflicts (Impact vs Rakuten). Needs a human to read the live affiliate directory entry; no account is to be opened by the project.

Grainger official API/developer portal: documentation, fees and account prerequisites not found; Punch-Out and ERP integration require an existing Grainger account and rep contact. No Home Depot API/catalog-feed documentation found beyond punch-out via procurement platforms. Ferguson and Dunn-Edwards official data routes not searched.

No standalone SKU price book found from cooperative purchasing (Sourcewell contracts are discount schedules). OMNIA Partners, BuyBoard, TIPS and state contracts for Arizona (State Procurement Office) and Nevada were not searched. Sourcewell 091422-WWG expiry (2026-11-08 vs 2027-11-08) must be confirmed.

GSA: no building-materials/HVAC/paint schedule price list identified; GSA open-data portal, catalog.gsa.gov help pages and any bulk export and reuse terms not verified. California DGS: only recycled exterior paint found; Cal eProcure pricing access and reuse terms unverified; no HVAC or general materials statewide contract found.

BLS/FRED: BLS copyright/reuse page and FRED terms not seen; BLS API data endpoint URL not seen; series IDs for softwood lumber, gypsum products, steel mill products, copper/PVC pipe and related PPIs were not retrieved (only ready-mix concrete FRED IDs and PCUBCON/PCUBHWY). No regional (Los Angeles) material price dataset with open terms found.

Classification: CSI full EULA text (MasterFormat, UniFormat, OmniClass) and current post-2026 platform terms not retrieved; UNSPSC commercial-use answer not retrieved; HS/Schedule B, SOC and CPV license terms were not searched (prior knowledge, unverified: HS codes are WCO-licensed but Census Schedule B and USITC HTS are US government publications; CPV is an EU Publications Office vocabulary). NAICS public-domain status not explicitly stated.

Manufacturer documentation not searched or not found: CertainTeed and Georgia-Pacific gypsum, standard 1/2 in. and 5/8 in. Type X weights/fire ratings, joint compound product data sheets (finish levels), screws/fasteners (box counts, per-sq-ft usage), Behr/Kelly-Moore/Sherwin-Williams product data sheets (spread rate, DFT, VOC), Sakrete yield, ready-mix specs (ACI 318/ASTM C94 are paid standards), CRSI rebar tables, SMACNA free duct references, HVAC manufacturer submittals (Carrier, Trane, Goodman/Daikin, Lennox), Owens Corning/CertainTeed insulation charts, and non-fiberglass insulation R-values.
Dunn-Edwards EVERSHIELD/VINYLASTIC/SPARTASHIELD spread rates and the conformance table contents were not visible in snippets.

Document-level reuse/copyright terms for all manufacturer PDFs (USG, National Gypsum, QUIKRETE, Dunn-Edwards, Johns Manville) are unknown; plan is to record cited factual specs only, not republish documents.
AHRI Directory public terms of use text not seen; commercial subscription cost not stated.
blocked_or_unverifiable: Sandbox network blocks retailer/manufacturer/BLS/government domains, so no page could be fetched and no robots.txt could be read directly; every item is search_snippet_only or prior_knowledge_unverified. Search results arrive as tool-written summaries: text inside quotation marks is literal, other text may be a paraphrase by the search tool. Evidence quotes are copied from those summaries.
Clause wording for Ferguson, Lowe's reseller definition and Home Depot (ampservices page) is the search tool's paraphrase of cached copies, not verified against live pages.
Affiliate commission rates, cookie windows and network identity for Lowe's/Home Depot conflict between blogs and were not recorded as facts.
FRED PPI values are stale cache values (Sep 2025 / Feb 2026) relative to 2026-10-24.
CSI February 2026 digital-platform and Uniclass CC BY-ND claims come from one secondary blog (wearenima.im) and are unverified.
Fee figures for MasterFormat licensing ($500 application, $1,100 minimum annual) come from anecdotal forum posts.
Retailer listing prices appeared in search results and were intentionally NOT recorded (no date/store/ZIP/SKU configuration).
Some URLs contain spaces exactly as returned by search (Quikrete data sheet, Sourcewell PDFs, hooverfence copy); they may need percent-encoding when used.
